citation_context: Despite a 171% surge in annual publication volume (increasing from 632 articles in 2020 to 1,713 articles in 2024), the average annual citations per article plummeted sharply from 8.53 to 0.93. This significant decline primarily reflects universal bibliometric patterns: On one hand, articles published in 2020 benefit from longer citation accumulation time (nearly 4 years), typically having passed their citation peak or retaining residual impact; whereas newly published articles in 2024 (which may have existed for only months at the time of statistics) are still at the starting point of their citation cycle, requiring time for their influence to materialize (time accumulation effect). On the other hand, the dramatic expansion in total literature volume (2024 being 2.7 times that of 2020) results in finite total citation resources being distributed across more articles, intensifying competition dilution effects (literature volume surge and competition dilution). Additionally, delays in citation database indexing and processing also lead to an underestimation of immediate citations for 2024 publications (database processing and citation indexing lag) [33].
